stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to steady energy and curb nuclear spread
body: The leaders of the US, China and Russia met together for the first time, in Shenzhen, China.
They said they want to stabilise energy flows and stop nuclear weapons spreading.
They also agreed to find ways to work more closely together.
stories.vc: Steadier energy flows would ease oil prices and help import-heavy India.

image.credit: President Bongbong Marcos / Presidential Communications Offi / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: World court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
body: The International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017.
It is the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide.
Myanmar must pay compensation, with terms set later.
stories.vc: The ruling raises legal risk for firms and investors dealing with Myanmar's military.

stories.headline: Houthi attack hits a tower in Riyadh's financial district
body: A Houthi attack hit a tower in the financial centre of Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh.
Saudi Civil Defence says it caused damage to the tower and nearby buildings, but no injuries.
Saudi Arabia condemned the attack.
stories.vc: Strikes on a financial hub could rattle investors in the Gulf.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps nearly 1,000 points to 83,022
body: The Sensex rose about 990 points (1.21%) to 83,021.75 on Thursday; the Nifty closed at 25,514.30.
Mid and small caps also gained.
The total value of BSE-listed firms hit a record ₹512 lakh crore.
stories.joke: Bulls are back, and they brought friends.
stories.vc: Record market value boosts the IPO pipeline, including Razorpay's.

stories.headline: Razorpay eyes a February IPO at about $5 billion
body: Bengaluru fintech Razorpay may publicly file its IPO papers as soon as next week, Bloomberg reports.
It is targeting a listing by February 2027 and a roughly $600 million issue.
The IPO could value it near $5 billion, below its $7.5 billion in 2021.
stories.joke: A down-round, but with a bell-ringing ceremony.
stories.vc: A big fintech listing would test investor appetite after Groww and Meesho.

stories.headline: Bengaluru has raised 47% of India's startup funding since 2010
body: Bengaluru startups have raised about $85 billion since 2010, nearly half of India's total, a new report says.
The city got 36.3% of India's AI startup funding.
It is home to 71% of India's AI and deep-tech unicorns, the Bengaluru Innovation Report says.
stories.joke: Traffic jams, yes. Funding jams, no.
stories.vc: Investors keep concentrating bets in Bengaluru, raising the stakes for its infrastructure.

stories.statLabel: Anthropic's first trade vs IPO price
stories.headline: Anthropic opens on Nasdaq at $111, 33% above its IPO price
body: Anthropic shares opened around $111.50, 33% above the $83 IPO price.
The offering raises over $81 billion.
With other funding, it expects about $220 billion in cash. (No new FT/Unhedged piece, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: A pop big enough to hear from space.
stories.vc: A strong debut tells investors the AI boom still has fuel.

stories.headline: Ex-Alibaba exec's Everful raises $48.5M to link shops with Chinese factories
body: Everful helps small retailers order from Chinese factories and handles delivery.
Vertex Ventures and January Capital led its $48.5 million Series A.
It ships over 5 million items a month to 60+ countries. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's deal.)
stories.joke: From factory floor to your shop floor.
stories.vc: Small brands get easier access to cheap manufacturing.

image.credit: Steve Jurvetson from Menlo Park, USA / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO is a jackpot for Amazon and Google
body: Amazon and Google, Anthropic's big cloud suppliers, hold stakes worth about $308 billion at the IPO price.
Amazon's 14.7% stake is worth about $159 billion.
Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft and others are also buying $26 billion of shares.
stories.joke: Selling shovels, then owning the mine.
stories.vc: Critics call it circular financing: suppliers fund customers who buy from them.

stories.headline: Stratechery: will ads pay for AI shopping agents?
body: Ben Thompson interviews analyst Eric Seufert about 'agentic commerce', where AI agents shop for you.
Seufert argues ads will be the answer.
Thompson says he wants retailers who cater to agents.
stories.joke: Even robots will see banner ads.
stories.vc: Whoever controls the shopping agent may control retail ad money.

stories.headline: Nadella explains why Microsoft offered 60,000 staff buyouts
body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he offered buyouts to give staff 'agency' rather than another big layoff.
He says the company is reorganising so everyone uses AI and manages it.
He says AI is changing software jobs fast. (No checkable Economist piece today, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Your new boss is an AI. Your new job: its boss.
stories.vc: Big Tech's AI shift is reshaping white-collar jobs worldwide, including in India.

stories.headline: Justice Nagarathna: women at the top doesn't mean equality for all
body: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, in line to be India's first woman Chief Justice, says a few women in high office don't prove equality.
Many women still miss out on education, jobs, property and justice, she said.
She spoke at Oxford's first Cornelia Sorabji lecture.
stories.joke: A glass ceiling crack isn't the whole roof.
stories.vc: Women's access to property and credit is key to economic growth.

stories.headline: AOC and Paris Hilton push back on AI deepfakes of women
body: US Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Paris Hilton spoke out against AI deepfakes that target women and girls.
The Defiance Act passed the US Senate 10 months ago.
It still hasn't been put into action.
stories.vc: Tech platforms face growing legal pressure over AI abuse tools.

stories.headline: Democrats move past 'Can a woman win?' after midterm sweep
body: Democrats' big midterm wins, many by women and candidates of colour, are changing ideas about who can win.
The question of a woman president has hung over three elections.
Many now say the sky's the limit for 2028.
stories.joke: Can a woman win? Check the scoreboard.
stories.vc: Women donors and voters are becoming the party's power base.

stories.statLabel: MitraClip at a South Indian govt hospital
stories.headline: Bengaluru's Jayadeva fixes a leaky heart valve without open surgery
body: Bengaluru's state-run Jayadeva Institute treated an 80-year-old woman's leaking heart valve with a MitraClip, through a vein.
It's the first such procedure at a government autonomous hospital in South India, its director says.
She avoided a risky second open-heart operation.
stories.joke: Heart repair, no chest opening required.
stories.vc: Advanced care at public hospitals saves patients big private bills.

stories.headline: AIIMS Delhi performs India's first open surgery on a baby before birth
body: AIIMS Delhi repaired a severe spinal defect in an unborn baby at 25 weeks, India's first open foetal surgery.
The six-hour operation took more than five weeks of planning.
It treated the most severe form of spina bifida.
stories.joke: Surgery so early, the patient hasn't been born.
stories.vc: New skills at AIIMS can reduce the need to travel abroad for rare care.

stories.headline: Ahmedabad Civil Hospital deploys 10 teams to fight drug-resistant germs
body: Ahmedabad Civil Hospital, with BJ Medical College, has deployed 10 infection prevention and control teams.
They will check infection practices and how antibiotics are prescribed.
It launched the drive during Antimicrobial Awareness Week.
stories.vc: Fewer hospital infections mean shorter stays and lower costs.

stories.headline: LMAX launches institutional perpetual futures for brokers
body: LMAX Group now offers institutional perpetual futures through Fintake's Helio platform.
Brokers can offer them next to FX and CFDs from one account.
LMAX says perpetuals make up most institutional digital-asset trading.
stories.joke: Futures that never expire. Unlike our patience.
stories.vc: Easier access could pull more brokers, and fast traders, into crypto derivatives.

stories.headline: State Street adds equity swaps to its prime services
body: State Street has added equity swaps to its prime services for big investors.
Clients can now get synthetic exposure to shares through total return swaps.
It starts with US and key European markets.
stories.joke: Owning the ride without buying the car.
stories.vc: More financing choices help hedge funds and quant traders scale up.

stories.headline: Explainer: What is a deal that never ends?
body: Imagine you and a friend agree on a price for a football card today, but you'll swap it later.
Grown-ups call that kind of promise a 'future'.
Most futures have a last day when the deal must be settled, like the end of a school term.
A perpetual future never ends. You keep the deal going by paying a small fee now and then to keep it fair.
This week LMAX said these never-ending deals are most of the big-money crypto trading, and it now offers them to brokers.
They're popular because they're simple, but you can lose money fast if prices go the wrong way.
stories.vc: Never-ending deals can mean never-ending risk.

stories.headline: F1 to get full-time stewards from 2027
body: The FIA will start moving to full-time F1 stewards in 2027.
It plans a panel of 12 to 15 permanent stewards.
The aim is more consistent penalty decisions, a long-running complaint in the paddock.
stories.joke: Finally, referees who know the rulebook by heart.
stories.vc: Consistent rulings protect the sport's credibility with fans and sponsors.
